subject.title: Improve doctor/gateway diagnostics clarity for mixed LaunchAgent/runtime states

question: Should doctor grow a consolidated final gateway diagnosis model that combines RPC health, service runtime/config drift, and channel conflict hints, and should that model expose a machine-readable diagnosis block?
rationale: Current main already collects many underlying facts, but the public state taxonomy, precedence, action ordering, and JSON shape are stable CLI/gateway UX choices that automation should not invent.

options.title: Add a final composed doctor verdict
options.body: Render one healthy/degraded/down diagnosis with probable causes and ordered recovery steps while reusing existing doctor, service, runtime, and channel facts.

options.title: Improve only the individual panels
options.body: Keep current independent doctor panels and refine specific misleading messages after live mixed-state proof narrows the confusing transcript.

options.title: Design structured diagnosis first
options.body: Define a compact diagnosis object and then render prose and optional JSON output from that object in a follow-up implementation.

recommendation.title: Add a final composed doctor verdict
recommendation.body: Render one healthy/degraded/down diagnosis with probable causes and ordered recovery steps while reusing existing doctor, service, runtime, and channel facts.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is central doctor orchestration and LaunchAgent bootstrap repair ownership across the relevant flow files.
